findings.shape: A selected European cream-white sessile lobed mass has dense shorter downward teeth over smaller connected lobes. It is distinct from the older broad-name North Carolina draft reference.
findings.surface: Original cream pigment and dense pendent tooth geometry; no generated photograph or source-pixel material. Lobes and tooth density remain a partial authored phenotype study.
findings.movement: Stationary same tooth-bearing body with greatly enlarged authored spore drift; no growth, decomposition, medicinal effects, measured discharge or airflow simulation.
findings.evidenceScope: Koga, Thorn and Langer2025 selected multilocus/taxon-context text separates European H.erinaceus from regional members of the former global complex. The old Alison Northup photograph is associated with a North Carolina occurrence and was retained privately, not relabelled by geography. New Henk Monster CC BY3.0 Wolfheze Netherlands2015 photograph was actually viewed and compared. The paper's NC-ND figures were not reused. Neither photograph was molecularly redetermined.
corrections: Replaced the broad-name North Carolina reference with a credited European photograph and exact original/derivative checksums.
Added smaller connected lobes and shortened/densified teeth after the first render showed overly smooth balls and a long beard.
Withheld the unreconciled broad-name GBIF map/counts from being displayed as narrow European species records.
findings.residual: Lobes remain too rounded and some upper surfaces too smooth; tooth insertion, maturation and cream/brown age variation are incomplete. The source-labelled European image is not a molecular voucher, and broad-name occurrence assignments still need specialist reconciliation.
